questions.question: An electric dipole is placed in a uniform electric field such that the dipole moment makes an angle of 60° with the field direction. The net force acting on the dipole is:
questions.explanation: A dipole consists of equal and opposite charges. In a uniform electric field, the forces on the two charges are equal and opposite, so the net force is zero.

questions.question: A point charge of +6 nC is placed in vacuum. The magnitude of the electric field at a distance of 0.3 m from the charge is approximately: (k = 9×10⁹ N·m²/C²)
Two identical point charges repel each other with a force of 10 N when placed 3 cm apart in vacuum. The magnitude of each charge is approximately: (k = 9×10⁹ N·m²/C²)
Two point charges of +4 μC and +9 μC are placed 20 cm apart in vacuum. The electric potential energy of this system is approximately: (k = 9×10⁹ N·m²/C²)

A 6 μF capacitor is charged to 24 V and then disconnected from the battery. It is then connected in parallel with an uncharged 3 μF capacitor. The energy lost during this redistribution of charge is approximately:
questions.explanation: Q_initial = 6×24 = 144 μC. Total C = 9 μF. V_final = 144/9 = 16 V. U_i = ½×6×24² = 1728 μJ. U_f = ½×9×16² = 1152 μJ. Energy lost = 576 μJ

questions.question: A uniformly charged solid sphere of radius 0.1 m carries a total charge of 5 μC. The electric field at a distance of 0.05 m from the center (inside the sphere) is approximately: (k = 9×10⁹ N·m²/C²)
questions.explanation: Inside uniformly charged sphere: E = kQr/R³ = (9×10⁹)(5×10⁻⁶)(0.05)/(0.1)³ = 2.25×10⁶ N/C

questions.question: A nichrome wire has resistance 12 Ω at 25°C. If the temperature coefficient of nichrome is 0.0002/°C, its resistance at 125°C is approximately:
A cell of emf 1.5 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is connected to an external resistance of 2 Ω. The current in the circuit is:
Two cells of emf 2 V (internal resistance 0.2 Ω) and 3 V (internal resistance 0.3 Ω) are connected in series opposing to a 4.5 Ω resistor. The current in the circuit is:
questions.explanation: Net emf = 3 - 2 = 1 V (opposing). Total resistance = 0.2 + 0.3 + 4.5 = 5 Ω. I = 1/5 = 0.2 A

questions.question: Two resistors of 6 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in parallel across a 24 V battery. The total power dissipated in the circuit is:
In a metre bridge experiment, the balance point is found at 40 cm from the left end when a known resistance of 10 Ω is connected in the left gap. The unknown resistance in the right gap is:
questions.explanation: Balance condition: P/Q = l/(100-l) → 10/Q = 40/60 → Q = 10×60/40 = 15 Ω

questions.question: A potentiometer wire of total length 10 m and resistance 20 Ω is connected to a battery of emf 4 V and negligible internal resistance. The potential gradient along the wire is:
questions.explanation: Current I = V/R = 4/20 = 0.2 A. V_wire = IR = 0.2×20 = 4 V. Gradient = 4/10 = 0.4 V/m

A series LCR circuit has R = 10 Ω, L = 0.2 H, and C = 50 μF. The resonant frequency of this circuit is approximately:
A series LCR circuit has R = 3 Ω, inductive reactance X_L = 4 Ω, and capacitive reactance X_C = 1 Ω when connected to an AC supply. The phase angle between the voltage and current is:
questions.explanation: Net reactance X = X_L - X_C = 4 - 1 = 3 Ω (inductive). tanφ = X/R = 3/3 = 1. φ = 45°. Since X_L > X_C, circuit is inductive and current lags voltage by 45°.

questions.question: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: EM spectrum by increasing frequency (decreasing wavelength): Radio > Microwave > Infrared > Visible > UV > X-ray > Gamma.

questions.question: Electromagnetic waves transport:
questions.explanation: EM waves carry energy (intensity = ½ε₀cE₀²) and momentum (p = E/c). They exert radiation pressure.

questions.question: An electromagnetic wave has a frequency of 3×10¹⁴ Hz. Its wavelength in vacuum is approximately: (c = 3×10⁸ m/s)
The amplitude of the electric field in an electromagnetic wave is 150 V/m. The average intensity of this wave is approximately: (ε₀ = 8.85×10⁻¹² F/m, c = 3×10⁸ m/s)
A concave lens of focal length 15 cm forms an image of an object placed 30 cm away. What is the image distance?
questions.explanation: Using the lens formula: 1/f = 1/v − 1/u. By sign convention, for a concave lens f = −15 cm and object distance u = −30 cm. Substituting: 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/(−15) + 1/(−30) = −2/30 − 1/30 = −3/30 = −1/10. Therefore, v = −10 cm. The virtual image is formed 10 cm in front of the lens.

questions.question: A plano-convex lens has a refractive index of 1.5 and a radius of curvature of 20 cm for its curved surface. The focal length of the lens in air is:
questions.explanation: Lens maker's formula: 1/f = (n-1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂). For plano-convex: R₁ = 20 cm, R₂ = ∞. 1/f = (0.5)(1/20) = 1/40. f = 40 cm.

A compound microscope consists of an objective of focal length 2 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 5 cm. The tube length is 20 cm. The magnifying power when the final image is formed at the near point (25 cm) is approximately:
A ray of light passes through a prism of angle 60° and experiences minimum deviation. If the refractive index of the prism material is 1.5, the angle of minimum deviation is approximately:
In a single-slit diffraction experiment, light of wavelength 500 nm passes through a slit of width 0.2 mm. The linear width of the central maximum on a screen placed 2 m away is:
questions.explanation: Angular width = 2λ/a = 2×500×10⁻⁹/(0.2×10⁻³) = 5×10⁻³ rad. Linear width = 5×10⁻³×2 = 0.01 m = 10 mm

questions.question: In Young's double-slit experiment, light of wavelength 600 nm is used. The slits are separated by 0.5 mm and the screen is 2 m away. If a thin glass plate of refractive index 1.5 and thickness 6 μm is placed over one slit, the fringe shift observed is:
questions.explanation: Path difference = (n-1)t = 0.5×6×10⁻⁶ = 3×10⁻⁶ m. Fringes shifted = (n-1)t/λ = 3×10⁻⁶/(600×10⁻⁹) = 5 fringes

questions.explanation: K_max = E_photon - φ = 4 - 2.5 = 1.5 eV (Einstein's photoelectric equation)

questions.question: A proton and an electron are accelerated through the same potential difference. The ratio of their de-Broglie wavelengths (λₑ/λₚ) is approximately: (mₚ = 1836 mₑ)
questions.explanation: λ = h/√(2mqV). For same V: λₑ/λₚ = √(mₚ/mₑ) = √1836 ≈ 42.8

In the Bohr model of hydrogen atom, the angular momentum of an electron in the n = 3 orbit is:
questions.explanation: Angular momentum L = nħ = nh/(2π). For n = 3: L = 3h/(2π)

A nucleus has a mass defect of 0.3 u. Its total binding energy is approximately: (1 u = 931.5 MeV/c²)
In the fission of a ²³⁵U nucleus, approximately 200 MeV of energy is released per fission. How much energy would be released if 1 kg of ²³⁵U undergoes complete fission? (N_A = 6.02×10²³ mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Number of nuclei in 1 kg = (1000/235)×N_A ≈ 2.56×10²⁴. Total energy = 2.56×10²⁴ × 200 MeV = 5.12×10²⁶ MeV

questions.question: In the fusion reaction ²H + ³H → ⁴He + n, the masses are: ²H = 2.0141 u, ³H = 3.0160 u, ⁴He = 4.0026 u, n = 1.0087 u. The energy released per fusion reaction is approximately:
In an intrinsic semiconductor at room temperature, the number of free electrons is:
options: A) Equal to the number of holes
B) Less than the number of holes
C) Greater than the number of holes
questions.explanation: In an intrinsic semiconductor, electron-hole pairs are generated thermally, so the number of free electrons equals the number of holes.

questions.question: A silicon diode in forward bias has a voltage drop of approximately:
questions.explanation: A forward-biased silicon diode typically has a voltage drop of 0.6-0.7 V due to the barrier potential.

The Boolean expression for a NOR gate with inputs A and B is:
questions.explanation: NOR gate performs OR followed by NOT: Y = (A + B)'. It outputs 1 only when both inputs are 0.

questions.question: A Zener diode with breakdown voltage 5.6 V is used in a voltage regulator circuit with a series resistance of 220 Ω. If the input voltage is 12 V, the current through the Zener diode when a load resistance of 1 kΩ is connected (in parallel with the Zener) is approximately:
questions.explanation: Load voltage = 5.6 V. Load current I_L = 5.6/1000 = 5.6 mA. Total current I = (12-5.6)/220 = 29.1 mA. Zener current Iz = 29.1 - 5.6 = 23.5 mA
